Checkpointing

Source: vignettes/articles/checkpoint.Rmd
checkpoint.Rmd

A nested Laplace fit solves one inner problem per cell of its hyperparameter grid, and a NUTS fit runs several independent chains. Either can run for hours, and a reboot or a killed job near the end would otherwise lose all of it. With control$checkpoint set, tulpa appends every finished cell or chain to a file; a later call with the same inputs loads what is finished and computes only the rest. This article turns checkpointing on, cuts the file the way a kill during a write would, resumes from it, and shows the file being refused once the data change.

Installation is covered in Get started.

library(tulpa)

Turn it on

control$checkpoint = list(path =, resume =) takes the file and whether to continue from it. With a path given, resume defaults to TRUE; resume = FALSE removes any existing file and starts over. The example is a binomial model with an intrinsic CAR field on a chain of 30 regions, fitted by nested Laplace through mode = "structured". fit_ckpt() wraps the call so the later sections can repeat it with other data or another resume.

set.seed(20260716)
S <- 30L
W <- matrix(0, S, S)
for (i in 1:(S - 1)) W[i, i + 1] <- W[i + 1, i] <- 1
df <- data.frame(region = factor(seq_len(S)))
df$x <- as.integer(df$region) / 10 + rnorm(S, 0, 0.3)
df$y <- rbinom(S, 20, plogis(-0.4 + 0.5 * df$x))

ckpt <- tempfile(fileext = ".ckpt")
fit_ckpt <- function(data, resume) {
  tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = data, family = "binomial",
        n_trials = rep(20L, S), spatial = spatial_car(W, level = "obs"),
        mode = "structured",
        control = list(n_threads = 2,
                       checkpoint = list(path = ckpt, resume = resume)))
}
fit <- fit_ckpt(df, resume = FALSE)
#> [nested-laplace] 1/9 cells (11%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells
#> [nested-laplace] 6/6 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells
#> [nested-laplace] 1/5 cells (20%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells
#> [nested-laplace] 5/5 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells
coef(fit)
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>  -0.2760639   0.4225753
full_size <- file.size(ckpt)
full_size
#> [1] 80349

The file starts with a header holding a fingerprint of the inputs: the response, trial counts, design matrix, offsets, the field’s structure and the solver settings. Each solved grid cell follows as one record, keyed by its hyperparameter coordinate and closed by a checksum over key and payload.

Resume after an interruption

A job killed while it writes leaves a file that ends in the middle of a record. Cutting the file to 45% of its bytes reproduces that: the records before the cut are intact, the last one is torn, and the rest are missing.

bytes <- readBin(ckpt, "raw", full_size)
writeBin(bytes[seq_len(floor(0.45 * full_size))], ckpt)
file.size(ckpt)
#> [1] 36157

The same call with resume = TRUE reads the intact records, detects the torn one by its short length or failed checksum, truncates the file to the last good record, and solves the cells that are not on disk, appending each as it finishes.

fit2 <- fit_ckpt(df, resume = TRUE)
#> [nested-laplace] 1/2 cells (50%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells
#> [nested-laplace] 2/2 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells
#> [nested-laplace] 1/5 cells (20%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells
#> [nested-laplace] 5/5 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells
c(size_after_resume = file.size(ckpt), size_uninterrupted = full_size)
#>  size_after_resume size_uninterrupted 
#>              80349              80349
all.equal(coef(fit), coef(fit2))
#> [1] TRUE

The file is complete again, and the resumed fit returns the coefficients of the uninterrupted one.

A changed input is refused

Resuming onto a file written for other inputs would mix cells from two models. Changing a single count changes the fingerprint, and the resume stops before solving anything:

df_changed <- df
df_changed$y[1] <- df_changed$y[1] + 1L
fit_ckpt(df_changed, resume = TRUE)
#> Error:
#> ! checkpoint: 'C:\Users\GILLES~1\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpMfzYdZ\file76404a1d41ad.ckpt' was written for different data or solver settings (fingerprint mismatch). Resume needs the same inputs + grid + control; use a fresh path or set checkpoint$resume = FALSE to start over.

resume = FALSE on the same path discards the old file and fits the new data from the start:

fit3 <- fit_ckpt(df_changed, resume = FALSE)
#> [nested-laplace] 1/9 cells (11%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells
#> [nested-laplace] 6/6 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells
#> [nested-laplace] 1/5 cells (20%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells
#> [nested-laplace] 5/5 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells
coef(fit3)
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>  -0.2341845   0.4000448

Sampler chains

The sampler kernel of mode = "hmc" takes the same control$checkpoint, with a chain as the unit. A chain is deterministic in its seed, its chain number, the data and the settings, so a resumed run returns exactly the draws of the uninterrupted one. The example is a Poisson model with a random intercept over 10 groups, four chains, cut at 60% of the file:

set.seed(1)
g <- factor(rep(1:10, each = 10))
d <- data.frame(g = g, x = rnorm(100))
d$y <- rpois(100, exp(0.3 + 0.4 * d$x + rnorm(10, 0, 0.5)[g]))

ckpt_chains <- tempfile(fileext = ".ckpt")
fit_chains <- function(resume) {
  tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = "poisson", mode = "hmc",
        control = list(n_chains = 4, n_iter = 1000, warmup = 500, seed = 11,
                       checkpoint = list(path = ckpt_chains, resume = resume)))
}
run1 <- fit_chains(resume = FALSE)
size <- file.size(ckpt_chains)
writeBin(readBin(ckpt_chains, "raw", size)[seq_len(floor(0.6 * size))],
         ckpt_chains)
run2 <- fit_chains(resume = TRUE)
identical(run1$draws, run2$draws)
#> [1] TRUE

The records are stored in the byte order of the machine that wrote them, so a checkpoint is for resuming on that machine, not for moving a fit between platforms. The fitters that take control$checkpoint are the nested Laplace doors (tulpa_nested_laplace(), tulpa_nested_laplace_joint(), fit_spde() and tulpa() when it routes to them) and the NUTS/HMC sampler; other sampler backends refuse the key.
